agents.one_liner: A WhatsApp agent that acts on every failed-delivery (NDR) event from Shiprocket or Delhivery. It fixes the address, reschedules the delivery, and moves COD buyers to UPI before the parcel goes back as RTO.
agents.buyer: Founder or ops head of a Shopify/WooCommerce D2C brand doing 300–5,000 COD-heavy orders a month (fashion, beauty, home, nutrition). The CX manager is the day-to-day user.
agents.problem: In India, RTO (return-to-origin) on COD orders runs 20–35%, and each one costs 2x shipping plus lost inventory time. Most NDRs die because the buyer wasn't home, the address was incomplete, or they changed their mind. Brands handle NDRs by hand in the courier panel, or with a dumb IVR that no one picks up.
what_it_does: Listens to NDR webhooks from Shiprocket, Delhivery, and Shipway, and reads the reason code (customer unavailable, address incomplete, refused, and so on)
Opens a WhatsApp Business (Cloud API) thread within minutes, in the buyer's language (Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Hinglish), using the order context
Collects a corrected address or landmark, a pin-drop, and a preferred slot, then pushes the NDR re-attempt action back to the courier API
For 'changed my mind' or 'price too high' on COD, offers a small prepaid discount through a Razorpay/Cashfree UPI link, with a cap the merchant sets
Escalates abusive or high-value cases to a human in Slack/Telegram with a one-tap approve or reject for goodwill offers
Posts a weekly RTO report by pincode, courier, and reason, with the rupees saved
agents.beyond_baseline: The obvious agent answers 'where is my order'. This one is triggered by courier failure events and writes the fix back into the courier system, so it saves money instead of deflecting tickets.
agents.wow_moment: Mark a test order as 'customer unavailable'. Within 20 seconds a Telugu WhatsApp message arrives. The demo user replies with a location pin, and the Shiprocket panel flips to 'Re-attempt scheduled' on screen. A counter beside it shows '₹186 RTO loss avoided'.
agents.price_inr: ₹4,999–14,999/mo, plus ₹10,000 setup. Or ₹15 per rescued order, success-fee only.
agents.stack: Python FastAPI, WhatsApp Cloud API, Claude API with a structured-output tool for the conversation state machine, Postgres, Docker on VPS, a small React dashboard
agents.integrations: Shopify, WooCommerce, Shiprocket NDR API, Delhivery, Razorpay/Cashfree payment links, WhatsApp Business Cloud API, Telegram for escalation
agents.first_customers: Shopify India D2C founder groups and communities on X and LinkedIn. Cold DM brands that show COD badges on their sites. Shiprocket-heavy agencies that can resell it. Offer a 14-day trial billed on success only.
agents.risks: WhatsApp template approval and conversation costs. Courier NDR APIs differ and some are limited. Buyers may hit opt-out, so use consent-based flows under DPDP. Shiprocket may build this natively, so move fast and add multilingual and prepaid conversion. Note: no market-signal URLs were supplied in the brief, so this pick is based on domain knowledge rather than cited sources.

agents.one_liner: A complaint-handling agent for NBFCs, small banks, co-op banks, and payment apps. It runs every failed-transaction complaint against the RBI TAT clock, calculates the compensation owed, drafts the reply, and builds the Ombudsman file before the deadline passes.
agents.buyer: Nodal officer, head of customer service, or compliance lead at an NBFC, small finance bank, urban co-op bank, PPI wallet, or UPI fintech app. These teams are 5–40 people and run Freshdesk, Zoho Desk, or Excel.
agents.problem: The RBI framework on harmonisation of TAT for failed transactions requires auto-reversal within set days, with ₹100 per day compensation for delays. The RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme also penalises weak grievance handling. Teams track these deadlines in spreadsheets, so they miss them, pay penalties, and get escalated.
what_it_does: Ingests complaints from email, Freshdesk/Zoho Desk, the app, and WhatsApp, and classifies them (failed UPI, ATM, IMPS, card, chargeback, mis-selling, unauthorised transaction)
Starts a TAT clock per category, computes the days elapsed and ₹100/day compensation due, and flags tickets that are about to breach
Matches the complaint to the transaction row in an uploaded CSV or reconciliation export (UTR, RRN) and states whether the reversal happened
Drafts the customer reply in plain language with the correct RBI references, for the officer to approve
Prepares the Ombudsman escalation pack: timeline, evidence, and response letters in a standard format
Produces a monthly compliance summary (volumes, TAT breaches, compensation paid, repeat complainants) for the board's customer service committee
agents.beyond_baseline: The obvious agent chats with customers. This one is a regulatory deadline engine with a drafting layer, so it saves penalties and audit pain instead of deflecting tickets.
agents.wow_moment: Paste in a messy complaint, 'my UPI payment failed 6 days ago, money cut'. The agent shows a red clock, 'TAT breached by 4 days, ₹400 compensation due', and a ready-to-send reply with the UTR matched. One click turns it into an Ombudsman-ready PDF.
agents.price_inr: ₹25,000–75,000/mo per institution, plus ₹50,000 setup for custom reconciliation mapping
agents.stack: Python, Claude API with strict JSON extraction and a rules engine for the TAT logic (rules in code, LLM for classification and drafting), Postgres, React, PDF generation, self-hosted Docker for data residency
agents.integrations: Freshdesk, Zoho Desk, email IMAP, CSV/SFTP exports from core banking or switch reports, NPCI dispute files, WhatsApp Business, Slack/Teams
agents.first_customers: Small NBFCs and co-op banks reached through compliance-officer LinkedIn groups. Fintech app founders. Offer a free audit: upload 100 old complaints and show the TAT breaches that were missed.
agents.risks: Selling to regulated entities means long cycles, security questionnaires, and data localisation. Rules must be verified against the current RBI circulars, not LLM memory. Never auto-send customer replies. Keep a human approval step and an audit log. No market-signal URLs were supplied, so this is based on domain knowledge.

agents.one_liner: A WhatsApp agent for corporate travel agencies. When an airline cancels or reschedules a flight, it contacts the traveller, offers rebook or refund options, and tracks the refund until the money is back.
agents.buyer: Owner or ops head of a small or mid-size travel agency or TMC (10–100 agents) that handles corporate or MICE bookings in India. Often runs on TBO, Amadeus, or Travelport plus Tally and WhatsApp.
agents.problem: After an IndiGo or Air India schedule change, agents spend hours calling travellers and chasing airlines for refunds. DGCA's refund CAR sets deadlines: 7 days for card payments, and up to 30 days when the ticket was bought through an agent. Agents lose track of refunds, margin, and client trust. Travellers message the agent at 2am.
what_it_does: Reads airline schedule-change and cancellation emails, or a TBO/GDS queue feed, and extracts the PNR, sector, old and new time, and traveller
Messages each affected traveller on WhatsApp with the new options: accept the change, rebook the next flight, or take a refund or credit shell. Fares are shown from the agency's search API
Records the traveller's choice and drafts the airline refund request or reissue instruction for the agent to approve
Tracks the refund timeline per PNR against the DGCA window, nudges the airline, and tells the traveller when the money should arrive
Notifies the corporate travel admin with a roll-up of which employees are affected and which meetings are at risk
Creates the credit note entry as a CSV for Tally or Zoho Books
agents.beyond_baseline: The obvious travel bot answers 'what is my booking status'. This one is a disruption workflow tied to refund law, so the agency stops chasing and the traveller never has to ask.
agents.wow_moment: Forward an airline 'schedule change' email. In seconds the screen shows 14 affected travellers, each with a WhatsApp message sent. A reply of '2' flips a row to 'Rebooking – 18:40 flight' and starts a refund countdown on the old PNR.
agents.price_inr: ₹7,999–24,999/mo by agency size
agents.stack: Python email parser with Claude for extraction, WhatsApp Cloud API, Postgres, React dashboard, optional TBO or Amadeus Self-Service API for fares, Docker
agents.integrations: Gmail/Outlook, WhatsApp Business, TBO/Amadeus/Travelport, Tally, Zoho Books, Slack
agents.first_customers: Travel agent groups on WhatsApp, TAAI and TAFI members in Hyderabad and Bengaluru, and corporate TMCs. Start with a done-for-you setup for one agency with a heavy IndiGo mix.
agents.risks: GDS and airline API access is gated, so start with email parsing. Airline email formats vary. Rebooking can't be fully automated, so keep a human in the loop. Refund rules vary by fare and booking channel, so verify against the current DGCA CAR. No market-signal URLs were supplied, so this is based on domain knowledge.

agents.one_liner: A support agent that watches your GitHub releases. When a bug is fixed, it finds every customer who reported it and sends each one a personal 'it's fixed' reply with a changelog link. It also catches new tickets that match a known issue.
agents.buyer: Founder, head of support, or CX lead at a B2B SaaS company with 5–50 staff, running Freshdesk, Zoho Desk, Intercom, or Help Scout. Strongest for Indian SaaS selling to global SMBs.
agents.problem: Bug reports go into a black hole. Engineers merge a fix, but nobody tells the 7 customers who complained. Support re-answers the same bug daily, and customers churn quietly. Existing AI helpdesk tools answer from the knowledge base but ignore engineering state.
what_it_does: Reads merged PRs, releases, and linked issues through a GitHub App or GitHub Actions workflow, and builds an internal 'fixed in vX' index
Clusters incoming tickets by underlying bug, using embeddings plus the LLM, and links them to the GitHub issue (or opens a new issue with repro steps, logs, and the customer's plan)
When a fix ships, drafts a personalised reply for each linked ticket, with the original problem, the fix, and a changelog link, and queues it for one-click approval
While a bug is open, replies to new matching tickets with a workaround and honest status, and tags the customer's account value
Updates the public help centre and a changelog draft from merged PRs
Weekly 'bug debt' digest: which open issues generate the most tickets and revenue risk
agents.beyond_baseline: The obvious agent answers from docs. This one connects support tickets to engineering state and closes the loop automatically, which no helpdesk bot does well.
agents.wow_moment: Merge a PR live. Seconds later a panel shows '9 tickets matched', with 9 drafted, personalised 'good news, it's fixed' replies. One click sends them all, and the helpdesk statuses flip to Solved.
agents.stack: Python, GitHub App and webhooks, GitHub Actions for self-hosted install, Claude API, pgvector for ticket clustering, Freshdesk/Zoho Desk/Intercom APIs, a React approval inbox, Docker
agents.integrations: GitHub, GitLab, Linear, Jira, Freshdesk, Zoho Desk, Intercom, Slack, optional Sentry
agents.first_customers: Indie hackers and Indian SaaS founders on X and LinkedIn, Product Hunt, and r/SaaS. Offer a free GitHub Action that posts the matched-ticket count on each PR, then upsell sending the replies.
agents.risks: Ticket-to-bug matching has to be accurate or it sends wrong 'fixed' messages, so keep human approval until precision is proven. Intercom and Zendesk may ship similar features. Customer data goes to an LLM, so offer a DPA and PII redaction. No market-signal URLs were supplied, so this is based on domain knowledge.

agents.one_liner: A WhatsApp support agent for regional ISPs and cable broadband operators. It diagnoses 'internet not working' by checking billing, RADIUS session data, and a photo of the ONT lights, then books the technician only if needed.
agents.buyer: Owner or operations head of a regional fibre or broadband ISP (2,000–50,000 subscribers) in India. Often a local cable operator or LCO with a small call centre, running Splynx, a MikroTik RADIUS server, or a local billing tool.
agents.problem: Most ISP support calls are one of five things: expired plan, area outage, router off, ONT showing a red LOS light, or a Wi-Fi issue. Calls are answered by agents who check three screens. Techs get dispatched for problems the customer could fix. Customers complain loudly, and TRAI's complaint redressal regulations require docket numbers and resolution times.
what_it_does: Identifies the subscriber from the WhatsApp number or an account ID, and checks plan validity, dues, and last payment in the billing system
Pulls the RADIUS last-session and uptime data, and checks other customers on the same OLT or PON or area for a mass outage, with a single proactive broadcast if so
Asks for a photo of the ONT/router and reads the LEDs with vision (LOS red, PON blinking, power off), then walks the customer through the right fix in Telugu, Hindi, or English
Sends a UPI payment link if the plan has expired, and reactivates the account after payment through the billing API
Books a technician slot with the full diagnosis attached if the problem remains, and issues a complaint docket number
Gives the owner a daily report of ticket causes by area and ONT batch
agents.beyond_baseline: The obvious agent reads an FAQ. This one checks live network and billing data, interprets a photo of the hardware, and filters out the tickets that don't need a truck roll.
agents.wow_moment: A customer sends a blurry photo of a router with a red LOS light. The agent replies 'Fibre cable cut or loose at your end. Your area is fine. Check this connector. Technician booked for 4pm if it persists', and the ticket appears on the owner's dashboard with the diagnosis.
agents.price_inr: ₹3,999–12,999/mo by subscriber count, plus ₹15,000 integration setup
agents.stack: Python, WhatsApp Cloud API, Claude vision API, Postgres, Splynx/RADIUS (MySQL or REST) connectors, Razorpay, Telegram technician dispatch bot, Docker
agents.integrations: WhatsApp Business, Splynx, MikroTik/FreeRADIUS, Razorpay/PhonePe payment links, a Telegram technician bot, Google Sheets as a fallback billing source
agents.first_customers: Local ISPs and LCOs in Telangana and Andhra, found through broadband operator WhatsApp and Facebook groups. Sell as done-for-you, starting with one ISP and a pilot for one area.
agents.risks: Each ISP has a different billing stack, so integrations are bespoke. Vision on LED photos needs testing across ONT brands (Huawei, ZTE, Nokia). Telecom margins are thin, so keep prices low. Avoid giving false outage claims. No market-signal URLs were supplied, so this is based on domain knowledge.

agents.one_liner: Drop in a trader's year of broker contract notes and get a CA-ready ITR-3 and tax-audit working file in minutes.
agents.buyer: CA firms and tax consultants who file ITR-3 for F&O and intraday traders, plus serious retail traders who do it themselves. Peak season is Jul–Oct, with the 3CD tax-audit deadline in Sept–Oct.
agents.problem: Every F&O trader's CA gets 250 daily password-protected contract-note PDFs from Zerodha, Angel, Upstox, Groww and ICICI Direct, plus P&L XLSX files. Turnover under the ICAI guidance, speculative vs non-speculative split, STT, charges and 44AB applicability are rebuilt by hand in Excel. Mistakes are common, and the AIS/26AS mismatch notices come later.
what_it_does: Unlocks and parses broker contract-note PDFs (PAN-based passwords, multi-broker formats) and normalises trades into one ledger

Computes F&O turnover as per the ICAI method (absolute sum of profits and losses, plus the futures and options rules), the speculative intraday split, and flags 44AB / 44AD / 44ADA applicability and the audit threshold
Reconciles broker P&L with AIS/26AS and bank credits, and flags gaps such as missing brokers, dividends and STT-only entries
Outputs a Schedule BP / Schedule CG-ready Excel, Tally journal import, and a draft Clause 3CD summary for CA review
Carries forward business losses by year and generates a WhatsApp query list for the client (e.g. 'missing contract notes for Aug 2024')
agents.price_inr: ₹499 per trader-year pay-per-file; CA plan ₹2,999/mo for 25 clients; ₹9,999/mo for 100 clients
agents.beyond_baseline: Generic invoice extractors can't read contract notes or apply the ICAI turnover rules. Existing tax tools stop at capital gains on delivery trades and ignore the F&O audit workflow.
agents.wow_moment: Drag in a folder of 240 password-protected contract notes. 40 seconds later you have the turnover figure, an audit-required flag, and a reconciliation showing ₹1.8L of missing STT credit.
agents.first_customers: Hyderabad CA firms, Telegram and X finance-tax communities, and the Zerodha Varsity / TradingQnA crowd. Offer a free first-year file for 10 CAs in exchange for testimonials.
agents.integrations: Zerodha, Upstox, Angel One, Groww and ICICI Direct contract notes and P&L; Tally Prime XML; Income Tax Utility JSON; WhatsApp Business API; Google Drive
agents.stack: Python, pdfplumber/PyMuPDF with per-broker templates plus Claude fallback for layouts, pandas, FastAPI, React front end, Docker on a Hostinger VPS, Telegram/WhatsApp intake
agents.risks: Broker PDF formats change. Tax advice liability, so keep it as a CA-review output with deterministic maths, not LLM maths. Handle PII under DPDP: encrypt files and delete after 30 days. No market-signal URLs were supplied, so none are cited.

agents.one_liner: Upload a health-claim rejection letter and policy. Get a clause-cited rebuttal, an insurer GRO escalation, and an Ombudsman-ready file.
agents.buyer: Independent insurance agents and POSPs, claim-assist firms, and HR heads at 50–500 employee companies with group health cover. Consumers pay per case.
agents.problem: Health claims are rejected or part-settled for non-medical reasons: a wrongly applied PED waiting period, an 'unnecessary hospitalisation' call, deductions for non-payable items, or a pre-existing disease raised after the 5-year/8-year moratorium. Policyholders can't read the policy wording or the IRDAI master circular. Agents lose clients when they can't help.
what_it_does: Reads the repudiation or deduction letter, discharge summary, final bill, policy schedule and wording, and extracts the rejection reason, clause cited, dates, sum insured and waiting periods
Checks the insurer's reason against the policy clauses and IRDAI rules (moratorium, standardised exclusions, cashless turnaround, claim-settlement timelines) and scores whether it is contestable
Drafts a point-by-point rebuttal to the insurer's grievance cell (GRO), with annexure list and timeline
Builds the escalation chain: insurer GRO → IRDAI Bima Bharosa complaint → Insurance Ombudsman. Computes the 30-day and 1-year limits and generates the Annexure VI-A complaint form
Sends the client WhatsApp status prompts and tracks deadlines, including the 15-day insurer response clock
agents.price_inr: ₹999 per case; agent plan ₹2,499/mo for 10 cases; HR plan ₹9,999/mo
agents.beyond_baseline: Typical claims AI helps insurers process or deny faster. This one sits on the policyholder's side and turns the policy text and regulations into an actionable dispute pack.
agents.wow_moment: Photograph a rejection letter on WhatsApp. In 30 seconds you get back: 'Rejection cites 24-month PED wait, but policy is in year 9, so moratorium applies. Draft rebuttal attached.'
agents.first_customers: LinkedIn and X insurance-agent groups, Policybazaar-style POSP WhatsApp communities, HR heads you know through enterprise contacts, and ombudsman-case YouTubers.
agents.integrations: WhatsApp Business API, Gmail, Google Drive, Razorpay, a PDF generator for the complaint pack, and optional agency CRMs such as Zoho CRM
agents.stack: Python/FastAPI, Claude with RAG over IRDAI circulars and top insurer policy wordings, OCR (Google Vision/Tesseract), WhatsApp Cloud API, React dashboard, Docker
agents.risks: It must not give legal or medical advice: label as drafting assistance with a clause-cited source for every claim. Policy wordings differ by insurer, so seed the top 8 health insurers first. Health data is sensitive under DPDP: get explicit consent and encrypt. No market-signal URLs were supplied, so none are cited.

agents.one_liner: Turn a bank's cheque return memo into a Section 138 NI Act legal notice, deadline calendar and complaint draft in minutes.
agents.buyer: Solo advocates and small law firms in tier-1/2 cities, MSME owners and traders with bounced cheques, and recovery agencies. Advocates are the paying users.
agents.problem: Section 138 cases are time-critical: the notice must go within 30 days of the return memo, the drawer gets 15 days to pay, and the complaint must be filed within 30 days after that. Missing a window kills the case. Junior clerks retype cheque details, memo codes, and amounts into Word templates, and mistakes in the notice get cases dismissed.
what_it_does: Extracts cheque no., date, amount, drawer/payee, banks, return date and reason code ('funds insufficient', 'account closed', 'payment stopped') from a photo or scan of the cheque and the bank return memo, plus invoice or loan documents
Validates the cheque's 3-month validity and the 30-day notice window, and flags limitation risk
Drafts the demand notice with correct facts, interest claim and 15-day payment demand in English, Hindi or Telugu, for advocate approval
Calculates the deadline calendar and sends WhatsApp/email reminders for dispatch (speed post/email), the 15-day expiry and the 30-day complaint filing
Generates the complaint draft with the affidavit and a document checklist (Section 200 CrPC / BNSS equivalent), and optionally an MSME delayed-payment interest calculation
agents.price_inr: ₹299 per case; advocate plan ₹1,999/mo for 30 cases; firm plan ₹7,999/mo
agents.beyond_baseline: Generic contract extractors don't understand limitation clocks and procedural steps. This is a deadline-driven workflow for one high-volume case type, not a legal chatbot.
agents.wow_moment: Snap a photo of a return memo. The agent returns a filled notice PDF with the dispatch deadline in red: 'Send by 14 Aug or lose the case.'
agents.first_customers: Hyderabad and Telangana advocates through bar associations, Telugu legal WhatsApp groups, CA and MSME recovery consultants, and chambers near the city civil courts.
agents.integrations: WhatsApp Business, Gmail, Google Calendar, Word/DOCX templates, India Post tracking, Razorpay, and Clio-style case managers (optional)
agents.stack: Python, Claude with deterministic date rules, python-docx, OCR, Telegram/WhatsApp bot, Laravel or React dashboard, Docker
agents.risks: Legal-liability concerns, so every draft needs advocate sign-off and the product should be sold only to advocates. Statute renumbering (CrPC→BNSS) needs care. Regional legal language needs review. No market-signal URLs were supplied, so none are cited.

agents.one_liner: Turns truckers' WhatsApp POD photos into matched LRs, shortage flags and ready-to-send freight bills.
agents.buyer: Small and mid-size transporters and 3PLs with 20–300 vehicles, whose accounts team chases drivers for PODs. Also freight forwarders and FTL brokers.
agents.problem: Transporters get paid only after the signed POD reaches the consignor. Drivers send blurry photos over WhatsApp, often late, and the accounts team manually matches them to LR numbers, e-way bills and Tally invoices. Remarks like 'short' or 'damaged' get missed, and invoices are delayed by weeks. Working capital is trapped.
what_it_does: Monitors a WhatsApp group or number for POD photos and PDFs, and extracts LR no., consignee stamp/signature presence, date and handwritten remarks
Matches each POD to the trip or LR and the e-way bill (EWB number, validity, vehicle), and flags mismatches or an expired EWB
Detects 'short', 'damaged', 'leaking' remarks and potential claims, and alerts the ops head before the bill is raised
Generates consolidated freight bills per consignor with POD attached, pushed into Tally or Zoho Books as vouchers, and emails or WhatsApps them
Chases drivers or branch staff for missing PODs with escalating WhatsApp reminders and shows an ageing dashboard of 'delivered but unbilled'
agents.price_inr: ₹3,999/mo up to 300 PODs; ₹9,999/mo up to 1,500; setup fee ₹15,000 for done-for-you Tally integration
agents.beyond_baseline: Standard OCR reads the document. This reads the delivery outcome and ties it directly to billing and cash, so the output is an invoice and a claim flag, not a data table.
agents.wow_moment: A driver sends a crumpled POD photo on WhatsApp. Within 20 seconds the dashboard shows LR matched, 'short 2 cartons' flagged, and the freight bill drafted.
agents.first_customers: Transport nagar clusters in Hyderabad (Bahadurpura, Kukatpally), Telangana lorry owners' associations, and FMCG/pharma 3PLs in the Hyderabad–Bengaluru corridor. Start with a done-for-you pilot for 3 transporters.
agents.integrations: WhatsApp Business API, Tally Prime, Zoho Books, Google Sheets, e-way bill/GST portal exports (GSP API or CSV), and TMS tools such as LogiNext and Shiprocket
agents.stack: Python, Claude vision for handwriting and stamps, WhatsApp Cloud API, Tally XML, React dashboard, Postgres, Docker on VPS
agents.risks: Handwriting and photo quality vary. Tally integrations differ per customer, so start with CSV and a done-for-you setup. WhatsApp Business API template costs and approval take time. EWB live APIs need a GSP. No market-signal URLs were supplied, so none are cited.

agents.one_liner: Stops retail chains from blasting email and WhatsApp offers for SKUs that the customer's nearest store doesn't have in stock.
agents.buyer: CRM or Marketing Ops manager at a 20-300 store apparel, footwear, electronics or grocery chain. Also D2C brands that run omnichannel stores.
agents.problem: Campaign ops teams build segments and send offers without checking store-level stock. Customers rush to the store, find the hero SKU out of stock, and the brand pays for the send and loses the customer's trust. Nobody reconciles campaign sends against inventory. No market-signal URLs were provided, so this idea rests on the builder's own enterprise CRM ops experience. I did not invent citations.
what_it_does: Before a campaign is scheduled, it pulls the offer SKUs and the audience, maps each customer to their nearest store by pincode, and checks store-level stock.
Flags the segments where stock cover is under N days and proposes a fix: swap the hero SKU, route to the e-commerce link, or suppress those customers. A human approves in Telegram or Slack.
Writes the suppression list or alternate-creative mapping back to the ESP or CDP (Netcore, MoEngage, WebEngage, Klaviyo) or exports it as CSV.
During the campaign, it polls stock every 30 minutes. If a SKU is about to sell out, it pauses later send batches and pings the owner.
After the campaign, it produces a one-page report: sends, store visits (if the POS is connected), stockout-hit customers, and the estimated wasted send cost saved.
agents.price_inr: ₹14,999/month per brand (up to 100 stores); ₹60,000 one-time setup
agents.first_customers: Hyderabad and Bengaluru regional chains the builder can reach through retail CRM contacts. Boutique CRM agencies that run campaigns for 3-5 retailers and can resell it.
agents.integrations: Shopify POS, Unicommerce, Increff, Zoho Inventory, Tally or Marg stock exports, Netcore, MoEngage, WebEngage, WhatsApp Business API, Google Sheets, Telegram
agents.stack: Python (FastAPI) workers, Postgres, scheduled GitHub Actions or cron on the VPS, Claude for the plain-English campaign risk summary, a small React dashboard, Telegram bot for approvals
agents.beyond_baseline: Not a follow-up bot. It's a pre-send gate that links two systems (CRM and inventory) that normally never talk to each other, with a measurable rupee-saved output.
agents.wow_moment: Drop in a Diwali campaign CSV. In 10 seconds a heatmap of store catchments turns red where the hero SKU is out of stock, with the line: '4,212 customers would have been sent to empty shelves. Fix applied. ₹38,000 of sends saved.'
agents.risks: Stock data quality varies, and stale feeds create false alarms. Writing back to each ESP needs a separate connector, so start with CSV and one ESP. Customer-to-store mapping depends on pincode quality. The DPDP Act applies to customer data, so keep processing in-region and minimise it.

agents.one_liner: Watches Tally purchase ledgers and warns accounts teams before a payment to a micro or small supplier crosses the 45-day limit under Section 43B(h).
agents.buyer: Finance head or accounts manager at a mid-size manufacturer (₹20-500 Cr turnover) that buys from many MSME vendors, plus the CA firm that handles their books.
agents.problem: Since FY 2023-24, Section 43B(h) of the Income Tax Act disallows the deduction for amounts owed to micro and small enterprises that stay unpaid beyond 15 days (no agreement) or 45 days (written agreement). Under the MSMED Act, interest is compounded monthly at three times the bank rate. Most manufacturers don't track which vendors are MSME or the age of each invoice. This is a real, dated, rupee-denominated penalty. No market-signal URLs were provided, so this rests on regulation rather than a cited link.
what_it_does: Connects to Tally Prime (XML/ODBC export) and reads purchase vouchers and outstanding payables by vendor.
Tags vendors as micro, small, or other using their Udyam number, and checks the number against the vendor master. Missing Udyam numbers are chased through a WhatsApp request to the vendor.
Computes the days left on every invoice (from the acceptance or deemed-acceptance date) and ranks which payments must go out this week to protect the tax deduction.
Sends a weekly cash-aware payment priority list to the CFO on WhatsApp or Telegram, with a one-tap approve that exports a bank payment file (CSV).
Before 31 March, it computes the likely disallowance (total overdue MSME amount × tax rate) and the MSMED interest exposure, and drafts the note for the tax auditor (Form 3CD clause 22).
agents.price_inr: ₹4,999/month per company; ₹25,000 setup with Tally connector; CA firms ₹1,499 per client company
agents.first_customers: Manufacturing MSME clusters in Hyderabad (Jeedimetla, Patancheru, Sanathnagar). CA firms with manufacturing clients, who will be asked to white-label it.
agents.integrations: Tally Prime (XML over HTTP / ODBC), Zoho Books, Busy, WhatsApp Business, Telegram, Google Sheets, the Udyam registration portal (manual verification or CSV)
agents.stack: Python Tally XML connector, Postgres, Claude for the audit-note drafts and vendor chasers (Hindi, Telugu, English), Laravel or React admin, Docker on a VPS, an on-prem Tally bridge agent
agents.beyond_baseline: Existing tools only show ageing reports. This one knows the legal clock for each vendor class and turns it into a payment priority list and a disallowance estimate in rupees.
agents.wow_moment: Connect Tally. A red banner reads: '₹1.84 Cr to 23 MSME vendors will become non-deductible in 9 days. Pay these 6 invoices (₹61 L) to save ₹19 L in tax.'
agents.risks: Rules on deemed acceptance and on what counts as a written agreement need CA review, so position it as decision support and not tax advice. Tally data mapping differs per client. Udyam classification can change, and a vendor's own registration may be out of date.

agents.one_liner: A WhatsApp agent that watches e-way bill validity against the truck's live position and acts before a ₹10,000+ penalty or a stuck consignment.
agents.buyer: Operations manager or owner of a transport company, 3PL, or fleet of 20-300 trucks. Also manufacturers who run their own dispatch.
agents.problem: E-way bills expire while trucks sit in traffic, break down, or wait at a border. Extension is only possible within an 8-hour window around expiry, and a vehicle caught after expiry risks a penalty and detention. After delivery, the signed POD sits in the driver's phone for days, which delays billing and payment. No market-signal URLs were provided, so this rests on GST rules and the builder's ops knowledge.
what_it_does: Pulls the day's active e-way bills (through a GSP API or a bulk Excel) and matches each to its vehicle number and the GPS feed or FASTag ping.

Computes the ETA to destination against the expiry time. If the truck won't make it, it messages the driver in Hindi, Telugu or Tamil asking for the reason, and prepares the Part-B or extension request for the dispatcher to approve.
Handles Part-B updates when a driver swaps vehicles (a WhatsApp message with the new plate triggers the update).
Collects the POD: after the GPS shows arrival, it asks the driver or consignee for a photo of the signed LR on WhatsApp, reads LR number, date and shortages, and matches it to the invoice.
Posts the POD status to the billing sheet or Tally and sends a daily list of 'delivered but POD not received' with the days of billing delay.
agents.price_inr: ₹7,999/month for up to 50 vehicles; ₹149 per extra vehicle; ₹30,000 setup
agents.first_customers: Transport companies in Hyderabad (Bowenpally, Medchal, Kattedan) and 3PLs around Pune and Bhiwandi. Fleet owners who already use LocoNav or Trackon GPS.
agents.integrations: GST e-way bill API via a GSP (Masters India, ClearTax, Cygnet), GPS providers (LocoNav, Fleetx, Trak N Tell), FASTag APIs, WhatsApp Business API, Tally, Zoho Books, Google Sheets, TMS exports
agents.stack: Python workers on the VPS, Postgres, WhatsApp Cloud API webhooks, Claude vision for LR/POD photo extraction, a simple React ops board, a Three.js or map view for the live fleet
agents.beyond_baseline: It joins three data silos that fleet tools keep apart (GST compliance, GPS, billing) and speaks the driver's own language on WhatsApp, instead of providing yet another dashboard.
agents.wow_moment: A live board shows a truck turning amber: '3h 10m left on EWB, 94 km to go, ETA 4h 20m.' The driver gets a Telugu WhatsApp message, the dispatcher taps Approve, and the extension is filed with no phone calls.
agents.risks: GSP API costs and onboarding delays. The extension rules have conditions (for example, circumstances beyond the transporter's control), so the agent must only prepare requests and the human must approve. GPS integrations vary by vendor. Drivers' phones and connectivity limit WhatsApp reliability.

agents.agent_name: CP Referee: Channel Partner Lead Ownership Agent
agents.one_liner: A neutral agent that registers, dedupes and time-stamps channel partner leads, then settles who gets the brokerage in 10 seconds.
agents.buyer: Sales head or CRM manager at a mid-size residential developer (2-10 live projects) in Hyderabad, Pune, Bengaluru or Mumbai. Also the brokerage firms that supply leads to them.
agents.problem: Developers get the same buyer through five channel partners, Meta ads and walk-ins. When the deal closes, partners fight over brokerage ('I registered him first'), sales teams quietly reassign leads, and CRM audit trails are weak. The result is brokerage disputes, partner churn, and wasted sales time. No market-signal URLs were provided, so this idea draws on the builder's CRM operations experience and Indian real-estate sales practice.
what_it_does: Accepts lead registrations from partners on WhatsApp or a simple form (name, phone, project) and hashes the phone number for matching, to reduce DPDP exposure.

Checks for duplicates against the CRM and existing registrations. It applies the developer's rules (for example, 60-day validity, a site visit renews ownership) and replies to the partner instantly with 'accepted', 'duplicate, owned by another partner till DD-MM', or 'existing customer'.
Logs every touchpoint (site visit, call, WhatsApp, ad lead) from the CRM into an immutable ownership timeline.
When a booking is made, it creates a brokerage-ownership certificate PDF with the timeline and rule applied, and notifies the finance team for the payout.
Warns the sales head about leads at risk of expiring and about partners who register and never follow up.
agents.price_inr: ₹9,999/month per developer (up to 5 projects); ₹40,000 setup; brokerages ₹2,999/month
agents.first_customers: Mid-size Hyderabad developers around Gachibowli, Kokapet and Financial District, reachable through agency contacts. Lead-gen agencies that serve builders and want to resell.
agents.integrations: Sell.Do, LeadSquared, Salesforce, Zoho CRM, Meta Lead Ads, 99acres and MagicBricks lead emails, WhatsApp Business API, Google Sheets
agents.stack: Laravel or FastAPI, Postgres with append-only event log, WhatsApp Cloud API, Claude to parse messy partner messages and write dispute summaries, PDF generation, small React admin
agents.beyond_baseline: It treats lead ownership as a trust and evidence problem, not a follow-up problem. The neutral, timestamped record is the product, and the CRM alone doesn't provide it.
agents.wow_moment: Two brokers claim the same buyer. Type the phone number and in 10 seconds a PDF appears: 'Registered by Partner A on 3 Mar 11:42, site visit 9 Mar, Partner B registered 14 Mar, duplicate. Ownership: Partner A.'
agents.risks: Rules differ by developer, so the rule engine needs to be configurable. Partners may resist a strict system. Disputes carry legal weight, so positioning is 'evidence record', not 'arbiter'. Needs careful DPDP consent and retention handling.

agents.one_liner: Turns every GST or Income Tax notice that lands in a CA firm's inbox into a triaged task, a client document request, and a draft reply skeleton before anyone opens the PDF.
agents.buyer: Partner or practice manager at a CA firm or tax consultancy with 50-500 GST and ITR clients (1-15 staff).
agents.problem: CA firms get scattered notices (GST ASMT-10, DRC-01, scrutiny, mismatch alerts; Income Tax 143(1), 139(9), 148 and e-proceedings) by email and portal. Deadlines are missed because the notice reaches the client first or an article files it late. Staff re-read the same PDFs to find the section, the due date and the documents needed. No market-signal URLs were provided, so this is grounded in the builder's knowledge of Indian compliance practice rather than a cited link.
what_it_does: Watches a shared inbox or a Drive folder where staff forward or upload notices, and reads the PDF with OCR.
Extracts the notice type, section, financial year, GSTIN or PAN, DIN, issue date and reply deadline. It sets the due date on a shared tracker and sets reminders at T-7, T-3 and T-1.
Matches the notice to the client and drafts a WhatsApp request to the client for the specific documents needed (for example, 3B vs 2B reconciliation, purchase invoices, bank statements).

Drafts a reply skeleton with the issue summary, relevant facts to be filled in, and an editable list of the sections involved. It never generates case-law citations unless they come from a firm-maintained library.
Produces a weekly partner view: open notices by deadline, client response status, and billable hours or fee estimate for each.
agents.price_inr: ₹2,999/month per firm (up to 150 clients); ₹7,999/month for larger firms; ₹15,000 setup including a template library
agents.first_customers: Hyderabad CA firms and GST practitioners reached via local ICAI chapter and WhatsApp groups. Tax consultants who handle MSME clients.
agents.integrations: Gmail or Outlook shared inbox, Google Drive, WhatsApp Business, Tally, Zoho Books, Zoho Practice, Notion or Google Sheets. GST and Income Tax portals via manual upload or email only, with no scraping.
agents.stack: Python with Claude vision/PDF extraction, Gmail API, Postgres, Telegram or WhatsApp bot, Laravel or React dashboard, Docker on VPS, hosted in India for client confidentiality
agents.beyond_baseline: It's a notice-to-action pipeline built around Indian tax forms, deadlines and DINs, instead of a generic document assistant, and it keeps the CA in control of every reply.
agents.wow_moment: Forward a scanned DRC-01 PDF. In 10 seconds: 'Section 73, FY 2020-21, reply due 14 Apr (11 days). Client ABC Traders notified, 4 documents requested, draft reply ready.'
agents.risks: Client confidentiality means a strong data-protection posture, with an India-hosted setup and DPDP-aware retention. OCR on poor scans can misread dates, so deadlines need a human-confirm step. The risk of fabricated legal citations must be kept out by design. Sales cycles with CA firms can be slow, but a low price and a free pilot help.

agents.one_liner: A WhatsApp agent that turns a portal or Meta lead into a unit-specific cost sheet, an EMI check and a booked site visit within 90 seconds.
agents.buyer: Channel partners, small and mid-size builders' sales heads, and brokerages in Hyderabad, Pune and Bengaluru that spend on 99acres, MagicBricks, Housing.com and Meta Lead Ads.
agents.problem: Real estate leads go cold within minutes. Sales teams reply late and ask the same budget and possession questions every time. Buyers want a real all-in number: base rate, PLC, floor rise, parking, GST, and stamp duty and registration. Telecallers hand-edit Excel cost sheets, so quotes are inconsistent and RERA details are sometimes missing.
what_it_does: Triggers on a new lead from a Meta Lead Ad, 99acres or MagicBricks email parse, or a webhook. It messages on WhatsApp Business Cloud API in under 90 seconds in the lead's language (English, Hindi or Telugu).
Qualifies the lead in 4-5 conversational turns: budget, BHK, possession timeline, home-loan need, and end-use vs investment. It scores the lead and flags NRIs and investors.

Generates a branded PDF cost sheet for the exact unit, using the builder's inventory sheet. It includes base price, PLC, floor rise, GST slab, state stamp duty and registration, the project's RERA number, and a loan EMI illustration.
Offers 3 site-visit slots from the sales team's Google Calendar and confirms with a map pin. It sends a reminder 2 hours before and nudges the cab pickup.
Pushes the lead, transcript summary and score to Sell.Do, LeadSquared, Zoho CRM or Google Sheets, and alerts the closer on Telegram with a 3-line brief.
After a no-show or a visit, runs a revival sequence (price-hold expiry, new-inventory alerts, construction-progress photos) with human approval for any discount language.
agents.price_inr: ₹6,999/month per project + ₹20,000 one-time setup; ₹1.5L/year for builders with 5+ projects
agents.beyond_baseline: Existing tools only qualify and book. This one produces the unit-specific, RERA-stamped cost sheet inside the chat, which is the document buyers actually ask for, and then runs site-visit no-show recovery.
agents.wow_moment: Submit a fake Meta lead form on stage. Ten seconds later the phone buzzes with a WhatsApp message in Telugu, then a PDF cost sheet for Flat 1204, Tower B, with the EMI and a 'Sat 11am visit' button.
agents.integrations: WhatsApp Business Cloud API, Meta Lead Ads webhook, Sell.Do, LeadSquared, Zoho CRM, Google Calendar and Sheets, state RERA portal (public project data), Telegram
agents.stack: Python FastAPI, Claude API with structured outputs for qualification and language switching, WeasyPrint for PDFs, Postgres, Docker on Hostinger VPS, a React admin panel for inventory upload
agents.first_customers: Start with 5-10 Hyderabad channel partners and mid-size builders in Kondapur, Tellapur and Kokapet, since you can visit them in person. Offer a 2-week pilot on one live Meta campaign and charge once response time and visit-booking rate improve. Then join builder and CP WhatsApp communities.
agents.risks: WhatsApp template approval and 24-hour window rules. Wrong pricing in a PDF is a trust and legal risk, so the agent must only use uploaded inventory and rates and include a disclaimer. Portals restrict lead API access, so use email parsing at first. DPDP consent must be captured. No market-signal URLs were supplied, so demand is based on domain knowledge and needs validation through pilot calls.

agents.one_liner: Paste a prospect's website or Instagram URL and get a branded audit, a personalised outreach message and a priced retainer proposal in under a minute.
agents.buyer: Founders and BD leads of digital marketing, performance, web and social agencies with 3-30 people, in India and selling to the US, UK and UAE.
agents.problem: Agency new-business work is manual. Someone spends 2 hours auditing a prospect's site, ads and Google Business Profile, then writes a generic cold email that gets ignored. Founders do outbound irregularly, so the pipeline is feast-or-famine. Generic AI cold-email tools send fluff, not evidence.
what_it_does: Takes a list of prospect URLs (Google Sheet, CSV or a Telegram message) and audits each one automatically. It runs PageSpeed Insights, checks for Meta Pixel, GA4 and GTM tags, checks the Meta Ad Library for active ads, scrapes Google Places ratings and review reply rate, and checks SEO basics.
Writes a 1-page branded teardown PDF with the top 3 leaks and an estimated revenue impact, using the agency's logo, tone and case studies.

Drafts a hyper-specific first-touch email, LinkedIn note and WhatsApp message that cite the exact finding, for example 'your Meta ads send traffic to a page that loads in 7.8s'. A human approves each in Telegram or a dashboard with one tap.
If the prospect replies or opens the audit, it generates a scoped proposal with 3 retainer tiers (INR or USD) from the agency's rate card and past deliverables, plus a Calendly or Cal.com link.
Logs everything to HubSpot, Zoho CRM or Notion and runs a 3-touch follow-up that adds one new insight each time, not 'just checking in'.
agents.price_inr: ₹4,999/month (50 audits) | ₹14,999/month agency plan with white-label PDFs | ₹30,000 done-for-you setup
agents.beyond_baseline: The baseline waits for inbound inquiries. TeardownBot creates the inquiry by sending proof of a problem, using public data on the prospect, so the first message is a gift and not a pitch.
agents.wow_moment: Paste a local D2C brand's URL. Forty seconds later a branded PDF appears with a red 'Your ads are live but your site loads in 8.1s' callout, a ready-to-send WhatsApp message and a ₹45k/month proposal.
agents.integrations: Google PageSpeed Insights API, Meta Ad Library, Google Places API, Gmail / SMTP, WhatsApp Business, HubSpot, Zoho CRM, Notion, Cal.com, Telegram
agents.stack: Python workers on GitHub Actions or a VPS queue, Playwright for tag detection, Claude API for synthesis, a React or Three.js animated score visual for the report, Laravel or FastAPI for the dashboard, Stripe and Razorpay
agents.first_customers: Use your own agency as customer zero and publish 10 public teardowns of well-known Indian D2C brands on LinkedIn and X. Then DM agency founders in Indian marketing Slack and WhatsApp groups and offer a free 10-audit trial on their own prospect list.
agents.risks: Cold-outreach compliance (CAN-SPAM, GDPR, TRAI/DND for WhatsApp and SMS), so send email and LinkedIn only for cold contacts and keep a human in the loop. Scraping limits and API quotas. Audits can be wrong, so they need confidence labels. Competes with tools like Loom-style audit services. No market-signal URLs were provided, so validate through outreach experiments.

agents.one_liner: It reads messy RFQs from IndiaMART, email and WhatsApp, including drawings and BOQs, and drafts a GST-ready quote for the owner to approve in one tap.
agents.buyer: Owners and sales managers of Indian SME manufacturers (fasteners, pumps, castings, sheet metal, packaging, electricals) with 20-300 staff who get 10-100 RFQs a week.
agents.problem: RFQs arrive as IndiaMART leads, Gmail threads with PDF drawings, and WhatsApp photos. One person decodes specs such as material grade, IS/DIN standard, tolerance, finish and quantity. They look up old quotes in Excel and Tally, calculate costs, and type a quote. Replies take 1-3 days, so buyers go to the faster supplier. Follow-up is rare, and win/loss reasons are never recorded.
what_it_does: Monitors the IndiaMART Lead Manager feed, a shared Gmail inbox and a WhatsApp number. It detects RFQs and extracts structured specs (product, material, standard, dimensions, quantity, delivery location, target date) from text, PDF drawings and photos.

Matches each RFQ to the product catalogue and past quotes (from Tally Prime exports or a Google Sheet). It flags missing information and sends the buyer one clarifying WhatsApp message, for example 'Is this EN8 or EN19? Need a test certificate?'.

Drafts a quote with the right HSN code, GST rate and place-of-supply (CGST/SGST vs IGST), MOQ, payment terms, freight estimate and lead time. It suggests a price band from the last raw-material rate and the target margin.
Sends the draft to the owner on Telegram or WhatsApp with 'Approve / Edit price / Decline', then issues the PDF quote by email and WhatsApp and logs it in Zoho Books, Tally or the CRM.
Runs follow-ups on day 2, 5 and 10 with sensible nudges. It records win/loss reasons and every month shows 'quotes sent, hit rate, margin leakage, top lost-to-price products'.
agents.price_inr: ₹9,999/month (up to 200 RFQs) + ₹35,000 setup including catalogue and rate-card import
agents.beyond_baseline: Generic lead qualifiers stop at 'meeting booked'. In manufacturing the deal is the quote, so this agent reads drawings and BOQs and returns a priced, tax-correct quote and not a chatbot reply.
agents.wow_moment: Forward a blurry WhatsApp photo of a bolt drawing plus 'need 5000 pcs'. Twenty seconds later the owner's Telegram shows a drafted quote with HSN 7318, 18% GST, a 'similar to Q-2231 sold at ₹6.40' note and an Approve button.
agents.integrations: IndiaMART Lead Manager CRM push API, TradeIndia, Gmail, WhatsApp Business Cloud API, Tally Prime (XML/ODBC export), Zoho Books, Google Sheets, SAP Business One (phase 2), Telegram
agents.stack: Python, Claude vision and PDF parsing with schema-validated JSON extraction, Postgres, a rules engine for GST and pricing kept separate from the LLM, Docker, a React approval dashboard
agents.first_customers: Pick one industrial cluster, such as Cherlapally or Jeedimetla in Hyderabad, and the Balanagar and Patancheru clusters. Do done-for-you pilots with 3 SME owners, using their last 50 RFQs as the demo. Then target IndiaMART sellers and local industry association WhatsApp groups.
agents.risks: Parsing technical drawings is error-prone, so keep the owner as the approver and never auto-send prices at first. Tally integration varies by customer. IndiaMART API access rules may change. Quote accuracy has contractual consequences, so the pricing logic must be deterministic. No market-signal URLs were supplied, so validate the pain with 5 owner interviews.

agents.one_liner: It watches product usage, spots accounts that are about to convert or churn, and sends the founder a daily briefing with the outreach already drafted.
agents.buyer: Founders and the first sales hire at seed to Series A B2B SaaS companies with a free trial or freemium plan and 50-5,000 signups a month. This includes Indian SaaS selling globally and Zoho-ecosystem products.
agents.problem: PLG SaaS teams have usage data in PostHog, Mixpanel or Segment, billing in Stripe or Razorpay, and a CRM in HubSpot or Pipedrive, but nobody joins them. Sales sees a signup only when it books a demo, so the best accounts, such as those that invited teammates or hit a paywall twice, go unnoticed and trials expire quietly. Generic 'day-3 tips' drip emails convert poorly.
what_it_does: Connects to PostHog, Mixpanel or Segment events, Stripe or Razorpay, and the CRM. It builds a per-account timeline with key actions, seat invites, integrations connected, pricing-page views, paywall hits and failed payments.

Learns each product's definition of 'activated' from past converted vs churned trials, and scores live trials daily with plain-language reasons, for example 'Acme: 4 invites, connected Slack, viewed pricing 3x, trial ends in 2 days'.

Sends a Telegram, Slack or WhatsApp digest every morning with the top 5 accounts to contact, each with a context brief and a drafted founder-voice email or LinkedIn note referencing real in-product behaviour.

Handles trial-ending rescue and dunning: for an engaged trial that is about to lapse it proposes an extension or a tailored offer for approval, and for failed Razorpay or Stripe payments it drafts a polite recovery message.
Writes the outcome back to HubSpot, Pipedrive or Zoho CRM as notes and tasks, and shows a weekly 'what behaviours predict paying' report.
agents.price_inr: ₹3,999/month (up to 1,000 trial accounts) | ₹9,999/month growth | ₹25,000 setup
agents.beyond_baseline: Typical agents respond to inbound forms. This one finds buying intent that nobody filled a form for, using product behaviour, and joins usage, billing and CRM into one daily action list.
agents.wow_moment: Connect PostHog and Stripe in 60 seconds. The Telegram bot then replies, 'Here are 5 trials likely to convert this week. #1 is Acme, with 4 invites and 3 pricing views.' The draft email reads like the founder wrote it, and a tap sends it.
agents.integrations: PostHog, Mixpanel, Segment, Stripe, Razorpay, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Zoho CRM, Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp Business, Gmail
agents.stack: Python ingestion jobs on GitHub Actions or cron, Postgres, simple gradient-boosted or rules-based scoring with Claude for explanations and drafts, React dashboard, Docker on the VPS, Stripe billing
agents.first_customers: Post build-in-public threads on X, Indie Hackers and Reddit's r/SaaS, and offer a free 'trial leak audit' on a founder's last 90 days of PostHog data. Also approach Indian SaaS founders through the SaaSBoomi and Zoho for Startups communities, and agencies that run PLG for clients.
agents.risks: The market is crowded (Pocus, Endgame, HubSpot PQL features), so a narrow niche and cheap price are essential. Small teams may have too little data for good scoring, so start with transparent rules. Each customer has different event schemas, so onboarding is the hard part. Customer data must be handled under GDPR and DPDP. No market-signal URLs were provided, so demand needs validation.

agents.one_liner: Upload a campaign export and get the true incremental revenue, not the inflated 'attributed' number, plus the segment to stop messaging.
agents.buyer: CRM/retention head or founder at a D2C or multi-store retail brand (₹10–500 Cr GMV) running email, WhatsApp and SMS on Klaviyo, MoEngage, WebEngage or Shopify Email
agents.problem: Platforms report last-click attributed revenue, so every campaign looks like a winner. Discounts cannibalise organic orders, over-messaged customers churn, and WhatsApp per-message costs rise. Nobody has time to build holdout analysis by hand, so the CRM team can't prove which sends actually earned money.
what_it_does: Pulls campaign sends, orders and customer lists from Shopify, Klaviyo, MoEngage or WebEngage exports/APIs, and from Razorpay or Shiprocket for COD vs prepaid and RTO.

Builds a synthetic holdout. It matches openers/clickers against similar non-recipients on RFM, recency and past discount use, then estimates incremental revenue and incremental margin after discount, WhatsApp cost and RTO.
Flags cannibalisation: customers who would have bought anyway and got a coupon, and fatigued segments where unsubscribes and complaints exceed the incremental gain.
Writes a one-page post-mortem per campaign with a plain-English verdict, and a suppression or segment list ready to import back into the CRM tool after human approval.
Sends a Monday digest to Telegram, WhatsApp or Slack: top 3 campaigns to repeat, top 3 to kill, and the ₹ saved by suppressing them.
agents.price_inr: ₹4,999/month per brand (₹25,000 one-time done-for-you setup for Klaviyo/MoEngage)
agents.beyond_baseline: The baseline agent answers 'what was open rate'. This one answers 'did this send cause the sale', using campaign-ops methodology from enterprise retail that dashboards skip.
agents.wow_moment: Drop in a Diwali campaign CSV. In 10 seconds the headline changes from '₹12.4L attributed revenue' to 'true incremental ₹3.1L, and ₹2.2L of it was discount you didn't need to give', with a red suppression-list button.
agents.stack: Python (pandas, statsmodels, propensity matching), Claude for narrative and verdicts, FastAPI, React report UI, Telegram/WhatsApp Cloud API for digests, Docker on VPS
agents.integrations: Shopify, Klaviyo, MoEngage, WebEngage, Razorpay, Shiprocket, GA4, WhatsApp Business, Telegram
agents.first_customers: Hyderabad and Bengaluru D2C brands and Shopify agencies you already know. Start with 3 free post-mortems on real campaigns, then sell to agencies who white-label it for clients.
agents.risks: Synthetic holdouts are estimates, so show confidence intervals. Data access varies by CRM; start with CSV upload. Brands need real order volume (>5k orders/month) for the stats to be meaningful. No specific market-signal URLs were supplied, so none are cited.

agents.one_liner: A CA's bulk tool that turns clients' broker tradebooks and contract notes into ITR-3 F&O turnover, a 44AB audit trigger, and AIS reconciliation.
agents.buyer: Practising CAs and tax-filing boutiques in India with 20–300 F&O/intraday trader clients, plus high-volume traders who want to self-file
agents.problem: F&O traders file ITR-3 with non-speculative business income. Turnover under ICAI guidance is the sum of absolute profits and losses, and it triggers 44AB audit thresholds. Brokers' P&L statements don't match what the Income Tax portal AIS/26AS shows. Charges, STT, expiry-day squareoffs, and multiple brokers (Zerodha, Upstox, Angel One, Dhan) make this a manual Excel nightmare every July.
what_it_does: Ingests tradebook, P&L and contract-note PDFs/CSVs from Zerodha, Upstox, Angel One and Dhan, and normalises them across brokers and financial years.
Computes F&O turnover per ICAI guidance, speculative vs non-speculative P&L, intraday equity, STCG/LTCG with Schedule 112A grandfathering, and brokerage/STT/other charges as deductible expenses.
Checks the 44AB audit trigger (turnover and the 6% presumptive-profit/cash-transaction conditions) and flags clients near thresholds during the year.
Reconciles against the client's AIS/TIS JSON, highlights mismatched securities transactions, and drafts the explanation notes for notices.
Sends clients a WhatsApp/Telegram nudge for advance-tax installments, with the computed amount and an approval step for the CA before sending.
Exports a CA-ready workbook and ITR-3 schedule values with an audit trail linking each number to source trades.
agents.price_inr: ₹1,499/month for up to 25 clients; ₹4,999/month for 150 clients
agents.beyond_baseline: Quicko and ClearTax serve one taxpayer at a time. This is CA-practice software that handles many clients, 44AB, and AIS mismatch notices in one place, and it uses your own domain knowledge of Indian markets.
agents.wow_moment: Drag 12 clients' broker files into one window. 20 seconds later you get a table with turnover, audit-required flag, tax payable and 3 red AIS mismatches, each with a one-line explanation.
agents.stack: Python parsers (pdfplumber, pandas), deterministic tax engine with unit tests, Claude only for notice drafts and anomaly explanations, Laravel or React dashboard, Telegram/WhatsApp bot, Docker on VPS
agents.integrations: Zerodha Console exports, Upstox, Angel One, Dhan, Income Tax portal AIS/TIS JSON, Tally (journal export), WhatsApp Business, Telegram
agents.first_customers: CA communities on Telegram and LinkedIn, ICAI branch groups, and trader communities on X/YouTube. Offer a free turnover calculation for 5 clients in a season-peak campaign (June–July).
agents.risks: Tax-computation errors carry liability, so use a deterministic engine and make the CA review the output. Broker file formats change. Sales are seasonal. No specific market-signal URLs were supplied, so none are cited.

agents.one_liner: Reads your Tally payables, spots MSME vendors approaching the 45-day payment deadline, and shows the tax disallowance you'd face if you don't pay.
agents.buyer: CFO, accounts head or owner of a mid-size manufacturer (₹20–500 Cr turnover) on Tally Prime, Zoho Books or SAP B1, and the CAs who serve them
agents.problem: Under Section 43B(h) of the Income-tax Act, payments to micro and small enterprises must be made within 15 days without a written agreement or 45 days with one. Otherwise the expense is disallowed until it is paid. Most manufacturers can't tell which of their hundreds of vendors are Udyam-registered micro or small units, and the year-end scramble is manual and costly.
what_it_does: Connects to Tally Prime over its XML/ODBC port, or to Zoho Books/SAP B1 exports, to pull purchase invoices, payments and the vendor master.
Classifies vendors as micro/small/medium using Udyam certificates and vendor-supplied details, and tracks the 15- and 45-day clocks from the date of acceptance or deemed acceptance.
Projects the disallowed amount and tax impact at 31 March, and ranks which payments to release first to avoid the highest tax per rupee paid.
Prepares a daily payment-priority list, with WhatsApp or email to the finance head for approval, and drafts vendor confirmation requests to fill missing Udyam data.
Generates the Form 3CD clause 22 working and the MSME Form 1 half-yearly outstanding-dues return for the auditor.
agents.price_inr: ₹3,999/month per company; ₹15,000 one-time Tally connector setup; CA white-label ₹9,999/month for 10 companies
agents.beyond_baseline: A generic reporting agent wouldn't know about the 15/45-day clocks, the Udyam classification gap, or the Form 3CD and MSME-1 outputs. This is built around one expensive, recurring compliance trigger.
agents.wow_moment: Connect Tally. The screen lights up: '37 MSME vendors, ₹4.2 Cr overdue or due within 12 days, ₹1.1 Cr at risk of disallowance, tax impact ₹27.7L', with a ranked 'pay these 9 first' list.
