agents.one_liner: Turns a class teacher's gradebook and attendance exports into personalised, parent-ready Parent-Teacher Meeting briefs and Hindi/Telugu/English WhatsApp summaries, 48 hours before PTM.
agents.buyer: Principals and academic coordinators of CBSE/ICSE/State-board private schools (300-2000 students) in Tier 1-2 Indian cities. Class teachers are the daily users.
what_it_does: Ingests exam marks, attendance and teacher remarks from Excel/CSV exports or ERP tools (Teachmint, Fedena, Entab, MyClassboard, Google Sheets). Maps them to CBSE competency-based assessment bands.

Per student, generates a one-page PTM brief for the teacher: 3 strengths, 2 concerns, trend vs. last term, and 3 talking points. It flags learning-gap patterns, e.g. strong in numeracy but weak in word problems.

Drafts a parent-facing WhatsApp message in the parent's preferred language (English, Hindi, Telugu, etc.). It is warm in tone and includes one home-practice suggestion and a PTM slot link. The teacher approves in batch before send.
Sends via WhatsApp Business API templates (Gupshup/Interakt) and tracks replies. It auto-books PTM slots and reminds no-shows.

After PTM, the teacher dictates a 30-second voice note on Telegram or WhatsApp. The agent turns it into a logged action item and a follow-up message, and flags at-risk students to the principal in a weekly digest.
Keeps all data pseudonymised before it reaches the LLM, with parental consent logging for DPDP Act 2023 (children's data rules).
agents.price_inr: ₹6,000 setup + ₹3,000-8,000/month per school (₹10/student/month)
agents.beyond_baseline: Existing school ERPs only dump marks tables and generic report-card remarks. This builds the human conversation around the data (what to say to this parent, in their language) and closes the loop through WhatsApp.
agents.wow_moment: Upload a messy marks Excel and 40 seconds later see a 40-student PTM binder. Tap a student and see a Telugu WhatsApp message to their mother that says exactly what to practise this weekend.
agents.stack: Python (FastAPI) + pandas for ingestion, Claude API for briefs and translation, React teacher approval dashboard, WhatsApp Cloud API / Gupshup, Telegram bot for voice notes plus Whisper, Postgres, Docker on VPS
agents.integrations: Excel/CSV/Google Sheets, Teachmint/Entab/Fedena exports, WhatsApp Business API, Telegram, Google Calendar
agents.first_customers: Run a free pilot for 3 low-fee private schools in Hyderabad/Telangana through personal network, with agency clients and school principals' WhatsApp groups. Charge a done-for-you setup per term. Sell to school chains' academic heads next.
agents.risks: DPDP rules on minors' data need clear consent and the data must not be sent unmasked to LLMs. WhatsApp template approval delays. Teachers may resist extra work, so the approval UX must be very fast. Messy ERP exports.
agents.wow_moment_note: Local-language parent messaging is the hook.

agents.one_liner: A Telegram/WhatsApp agent for JEE/NEET/UPSC coaching institutes. Students photograph a wrong test answer and the agent diagnoses the type of mistake (concept gap, silly error, time pressure, misread question). It then builds each student's personal error notebook and a weekly 20-question retry set.
agents.buyer: Owners and academic heads of mid-size coaching institutes (200-3000 students) in Kota, Hyderabad, Delhi, Vijayawada, plus independent test-series creators on Telegram.
what_it_does: Imports test-series results (OMR CSV, Testbook/Classplus/Teachmint exports or an answer-key PDF) and maps each question to a chapter and topic tag.

Student sends a photo of their working or taps a question number in Telegram. The agent classifies the error (concept, calculation, silly, misread, guess, time pressure) and gives a 3-line fix, not the full solution.

Maintains a spaced-repetition error notebook per student. Every Sunday it generates a personalised 20-question retry set from the institute's own question bank, weighted to the student's top error types.
Gives faculty a heatmap, e.g. '62% of batch B lost marks on Rotational Motion through sign errors, not concept gaps'. It also drafts a 10-minute doubt-class plan.
Sends parents a monthly WhatsApp progress note with error-type trends, with faculty approval first.
Flags students whose guess-rate or time-pressure errors rise before big mocks, so mentors can intervene.
agents.price_inr: ₹4,999-14,999/month per institute (₹40/active student/month); ₹999 per student for independent test-series creators
agents.beyond_baseline: Typical AI tutors solve the question. This diagnoses WHY the student got it wrong and builds institute-specific, batch-level analytics from the institute's own test data, which is what faculty pay for.
agents.wow_moment: Photograph a wrong physics answer. In 8 seconds the bot replies 'Sign error at step 3, your 4th this month in Rotational Motion' and adds it to a notebook that has a one-tap retry set.
agents.stack: Telegram bot (python-telegram-bot), Claude vision for handwritten work, Postgres, pandas for test imports, React faculty heatmap dashboard, GitHub Actions cron for weekly sets, Hostinger VPS Docker
agents.integrations: Telegram, WhatsApp Business API, Google Sheets/CSV OMR exports, Classplus/Testbook/Teachmint exports, institute question-bank PDFs
agents.first_customers: Hyderabad (Ameerpet/Kukatpally) JEE/NEET and TSPSC/UPSC coaching institutes via direct demos. Offer one-batch free pilots, then target Telegram test-series creators who already run paid channels.
agents.risks: Handwriting OCR on messy work is imperfect, so allow student corrections. Faculty may distrust diagnoses. Question-bank copyright, so only use the institute's own material. Student minors' data under DPDP.

agents.one_liner: Turns a company's changing compliance documents (POSH, RBI KYC circulars, IRDAI updates, SOPs) into scenario-based WhatsApp/Teams micro-drills for frontline staff. It produces audit-ready completion evidence for compliance and L&D heads.
agents.buyer: L&D and compliance heads at Indian NBFCs, insurance distributors, banks' branch networks, retail chains, BPOs and staffing firms (200-5000 frontline staff).
what_it_does: Monitors a watched folder, SharePoint, or email inbox for new circulars and SOP PDFs (e.g. RBI master directions, IRDAI circulars, internal policy updates). It summarises what changed versus the previous version.

Generates 5 scenario-based micro-drills per change in the staff's context (e.g. a branch officer facing a customer with a mismatched PAN) with right/wrong rationale, in English and regional languages. The compliance head approves before release.
Delivers drills through WhatsApp Business, Microsoft Teams or Telegram at randomised times, 2 minutes each, and nudges non-responders using manager escalation rules.
Scores each employee per policy and finds weak areas by branch or team. It then auto-sends targeted refreshers to only those who failed.
Exports an audit-ready evidence pack (who was trained on which policy version, when, score, retries) in PDF/Excel for RBI/IRDAI inspections and internal audit, with DPDP-compliant retention.
Syncs completions to the HRMS/LMS (Zoho People, Keka, greytHR, Moodle) via CSV/API.
agents.price_inr: ₹25,000 setup + ₹15,000-60,000/month depending on headcount (₹40-100/employee/year)
agents.beyond_baseline: LMS tools deliver long annual courses nobody remembers. This reacts to the exact regulatory change within days, tests judgment through scenarios rather than quizzes, and produces inspection-ready evidence of version-wise training.
agents.wow_moment: Drop in a real RBI circular PDF. 60 seconds later a colleague's WhatsApp receives a 'customer at the counter' scenario with a tap-to-answer reply, and the compliance dashboard shows version-wise completion live.
agents.stack: Python workers, Claude API for diffing and scenario generation, WhatsApp Cloud API/Gupshup, MS Teams webhooks, Laravel or React admin with approval workflow, Postgres, PDF/Excel export, Docker on VPS
agents.integrations: WhatsApp Business, Microsoft Teams, Telegram, SharePoint/Google Drive, Zoho People, Keka, greytHR, Moodle, email inbox via IMAP
agents.first_customers: Start with done-for-you pilots at NBFCs, microfinance firms and insurance agencies in Hyderabad. They have large frontline staff and heavy compliance pressure. Reach out to compliance officers on LinkedIn with a 'your latest circular, as a drill' demo.
agents.risks: Wrong scenarios could teach wrong compliance, so keep human approval and source citations for every drill. Long enterprise sales cycles and security reviews. WhatsApp business verification and costs. Employee data privacy.

agents.one_liner: Turns a GP or specialist clinic's old patient records into a WhatsApp recall engine. It finds chronic patients who are overdue for a refill, HbA1c or BP review and books them back in, in Telugu, Hindi or English.
agents.buyer: Owner-doctors and practice managers at single-doctor and 2-10 doctor clinics. Diabetology, cardiology, dermatology, fertility and paediatrics (vaccine schedules) are the best fits. Also multi-branch clinic chains of 3-20 sites.
agents.problem: Small clinics lose a large share of revenue because chronic patients quietly drop off after 1-2 visits. Front desks only handle inbound calls. EMRs such as Practo Ray, Eka Care or Clinic software hold the data but do no outbound lifecycle marketing. Generic WhatsApp blast tools ignore clinical logic. Under DPDP, clinics also need provable consent for every message.
what_it_does: Ingests a CSV/Excel export or API feed from Practo Ray, Eka Care or Google Sheets. It reads the last visit, diagnosis tags and prescription duration (e.g. '30 days Metformin') to compute due dates for refills, follow-ups and tests.

Segments patients like a CRM lifecycle journey: overdue 7/30/90 days, high-value, and missed-appointment cohorts. It builds a daily recall list for the front desk to approve, with a one-tap 'send all'.

Sends WhatsApp Business Cloud API template messages in the patient's preferred language. Patients reply with a slot button and the agent books it into Google Calendar or the EMR queue. If a patient replies 'chest pain', the agent skips booking and alerts the clinic staff on Telegram.
Records DPDP-style consent and opt-out for each patient, with a timestamped log and a one-click erasure request.
Weekly Telegram or WhatsApp report to the doctor: patients recalled, bookings made and estimated revenue recovered in ₹. The doctor can see the payoff at a glance.
agents.price_inr: ₹2,999/month per clinic; ₹14,999 one-time setup for done-for-you EMR import and template approval; ₹7,999/month for chains with up to 5 branches
agents.first_customers: Start with 10 diabetology and dermatology clinics in Hyderabad through personal outreach and doctor WhatsApp groups. Offer a free 'lost patients audit' on their CSV that shows the ₹ value of lapsed patients. Then partner with clinic-software resellers and local IMA chapters.
agents.integrations: WhatsApp Business Cloud API, Practo Ray / Eka Care / Healthray CSV exports, Google Calendar and Sheets, Razorpay (optional advance booking fee), Telegram for staff alerts, ABDM/ABHA ID capture (phase 2)
agents.beyond_baseline: The baseline agent answers inbound queries and books appointments. This one starts outbound conversations from clinical logic such as prescription duration and condition-based review cycles. It uses the builder's CRM campaign-ops skills (segmentation, cadences, suppression) in a market that has no real lifecycle tooling.
agents.wow_moment: Drag a messy EMR CSV onto the page. In 10 seconds the dashboard shows '312 patients overdue. Estimated recoverable revenue ₹4.8L'. Click 'Send', and a phone mock-up shows a Telugu WhatsApp message from the clinic. Tapping 'Tomorrow 6pm' updates the calendar live.
agents.stack: Python (FastAPI) + Claude API for language, intent classification and template drafting; React dashboard; Postgres; WhatsApp Cloud API; Docker on Hostinger VPS; GitHub Actions for scheduled daily recall jobs
agents.risks: WhatsApp template approval and quality rating can limit sending, so start with low volumes. Medical advice must never be generated, so use fixed clinical rules and approved copy only. Every EMR export format differs, so ship a column-mapping UI. Patient data is sensitive, so use encryption, a data-processing agreement and a consent-first design. No market-signal URLs were supplied in the brief, so none are cited.

agents.one_liner: Handles the TPA and insurer back-and-forth for cashless claims. It drafts pre-auth requests, answers TPA queries with evidence from the patient file, and chases pending claims, so insurance desk staff stop re-typing and losing money to deductions.
agents.buyer: Insurance and TPA desk heads, billing managers and CFOs at 30-300 bed private hospitals and nursing homes in tier 1-2 Indian cities. They are the ones who see the cost of claim rejections.
agents.problem: Cashless claims run through email and TPA portals (Medi Assist, Paramount, MDIndia, Health India, Star, HDFC Ergo). Each TPA has its own checklist. Staff re-type clinical data from the HIS into pre-auth forms. TPA 'query' and 'deficiency' emails lead to delays, partial approvals and deductions. Discharge is delayed while patients wait for approval. NHCX and PM-JAY/Ayushman Bharat packages add further paperwork.
what_it_does: Watches the insurance desk's shared inbox (IMAP/Gmail). It classifies each TPA email as approval, query, enhancement, rejection or settlement, and links it to the patient and claim ID.

Reads the admission note, investigation reports and doctor notes (PDF/photo OCR). It drafts the pre-auth with the diagnosis, procedure and expected stay, suggests ICD-10 and package codes, and lists missing mandatory documents per TPA checklist before submission.

For TPA queries such as 'Please provide the indication for admission and an ECG', it drafts a reply. The reply cites the exact lines and attachments from the file as evidence, and the desk approves it with one click.
Flags likely deductions in advance. These include room rent proportionate deduction, non-payable items and missing investigation justification. The desk can then fix them before discharge.
Keeps a live claim TAT board. It escalates claims pending past a set number of hours, auto-prepares the final discharge bundle and posts a daily 'money stuck in claims' digest to the CFO on WhatsApp.
agents.price_inr: ₹25,000/month for a 100-bed hospital; ₹75,000-1,50,000 one-time pilot setup with TPA template customisation; ₹2,000 per month per extra TPA workflow
agents.first_customers: Use the builder's network to target 3 nursing homes and mid-size hospitals in Hyderabad. Offer a 30-day paid pilot on query-reply drafting only, since it needs no HIS integration and just an inbox. Measure approval TAT and deduction ₹ saved, then use the case study to sell to hospital groups and consultants who run TPA desk outsourcing.
agents.integrations: Gmail/Outlook (IMAP/Graph) for TPA emails, WhatsApp Business, HIS exports (Insta, KareXpert, Medixcel, Marg HIS), TPA portals via semi-manual upload (RPA phase 2), NHCX FHIR sandbox (phase 2), Google Drive/S3 document store
agents.beyond_baseline: The baseline handles appointments and intake forms, which are front-of-house tasks. This agent targets the back-office revenue leak where a hospital's cash is actually stuck. It starts from the inbox rather than an HIS API, so it can ship without a hard integration.
agents.wow_moment: Forward a real-looking TPA query email, with names redacted. In 10 seconds a reply appears with the clinical justification and the supporting PDF page highlighted as evidence. A banner shows 'Likely deduction avoided: ₹18,400'. One click sends the reply.
agents.stack: Python + Claude API with structured extraction and PDF/vision OCR; Laravel or React admin; Postgres + pgvector for the patient document index; IMAP polling; Docker on VPS; human-in-the-loop approval queue; audit logs
agents.risks: Hospital sales cycles are long and need IT and legal sign-off. A wrong ICD or package code could cause claim rejection, so keep a human approver and show confidence scores. Patient health data needs DPDP-grade security and ideally on-premise or India-region hosting. Every TPA format differs, so start with 2-3 TPAs. No market-signal URLs were supplied in the brief, so none are cited.

agents.one_liner: Watches the LIS result feed for critical values and breached report turnaround times. It reaches the referring doctor on WhatsApp, voice or Telegram, records read-back acknowledgment, and generates the NABL audit trail.
agents.buyer: Lab directors, pathologists and quality managers at NABL-accredited or NABL-aspiring diagnostic centres and chains with 3-30 collection centres.
agents.problem: NABL (ISO 15189) requires that critical results are communicated to a clinician quickly, with time, person and read-back documented. In most labs this is done by phone calls and handwritten registers, so records are patchy and audits are stressful. Late reports and unreachable doctors also hurt patient safety and reputation. LIS systems like Medsoft, Labsys, Tulip or Healthray store results but rarely escalate or track acknowledgment.
what_it_does: Polls the LIS database, HL7 messages or a scheduled CSV export. It matches each result against configured critical limits (e.g. K+ >6.5, Hb <5, troponin positive, platelets <20k) with the lab's own ranges per age and sex.

Alerts instantly on WhatsApp or by voice call (Exotel/Twilio IVR) to the referring doctor and to the pathologist on Telegram. The message contains patient ID, test, value and a one-tap 'Acknowledged' button. The pathologist verifies the result before anything is sent.

Escalates automatically along a ladder if there is no acknowledgment in 10 minutes. It goes from doctor, to the doctor's clinic, to the patient (with safe, non-diagnostic wording), to the lab head. Every step is timestamped.
Tracks TAT per test against promised report time. It predicts delays from the sample queue and alerts the centre manager before a breach. It also auto-updates patients on WhatsApp with a new ETA.
Produces a one-click NABL audit pack as a PDF/Excel. It lists the critical-value log, TAT breach analysis and corrective-action notes, drafted for quality manager approval.
agents.price_inr: ₹6,999/month per lab; ₹3,999/month per additional collection centre; ₹20,000 one-time LIS connector setup
agents.first_customers: Approach 5-10 mid-size pathology labs in Hyderabad and Telangana that are preparing for NABL renewal. Pitch the audit pack as the deliverable. Offer a free 2-week shadow mode with replayed results. Later sell via LIS vendors and NABL consultants, who get a referral fee.
agents.integrations: LIS (Medsoft, Labsys, Tulip, Healthray, custom MySQL/SQL Server), HL7 v2 and CSV, WhatsApp Business Cloud API, Exotel/Twilio voice, Telegram bot for pathologists, Google Sheets, ABDM/ABHA (phase 2)
agents.beyond_baseline: The baseline handles appointments and intake, which most booking tools already do. This agent sits on the clinical-safety and compliance path and produces evidence an auditor asks for. It converts a dull compliance obligation into an automatic, provable workflow.
agents.wow_moment: Insert a fake lab result row with 'Potassium 7.1'. Within 15 seconds the doctor's phone shows a WhatsApp alert and rings through voice, and the dashboard timeline lights up. When the 'Acknowledged' button is tapped, a NABL-ready log line appears with all timestamps.
agents.stack: Python workers for DB polling and HL7 parsing; rules engine for critical limits (LLM only for message drafting and audit narrative, never for deciding clinical thresholds); React dashboard; WhatsApp and Exotel APIs; Telegram bot; Postgres; Docker on VPS
agents.risks: Patient-safety liability, so use deterministic rules, pathologist verification and clear fail-safes with an uptime alert if polling stops. Every LIS has a different schema and access rules, so begin with CSV or DB-read-only access. Voice and WhatsApp deliverability varies. Needs DPDP-compliant handling of lab data and a signed agreement. No market-signal URLs were supplied in the brief, so none are cited.

agents.one_liner: Forward a customer PO on WhatsApp and get a BOM-exploded shortage list, a realistic ship date, and vendor RFQs in 30 seconds.
agents.buyer: Owner or purchase head of a 20-200 person Indian MSME job shop (auto components, fabrication, electrical panels, plastics). They run on Tally Prime or Zoho Inventory plus Excel BOMs.
agents.problem: MSME owners find out a raw material or bought-out part is missing only after promising the customer a delivery date. BOMs live in Excel, stock lives in Tally, and open POs live in WhatsApp chats. Late payments to micro and small suppliers now carry a cost under Sec 43B(h), which requires payment within 45 days. Because of that, buying decisions also have to consider cash and payables, not just stock. Note: no market-signal URLs were supplied in the prompt, so none are cited.
what_it_does: Reads an incoming PO (PDF, image or Excel, forwarded on WhatsApp or email) and matches line items to BOM masters using an LLM with fuzzy part-number matching.

Explodes the BOM and nets it against Tally stock, open purchase orders and other committed sales orders. It outputs a per-order shortage table and a promised-date feasibility check using vendor lead times learned from past GRNs.

Drafts RFQ or PO messages for the shortage items in English, Hindi or Telugu. These go to the vendor's WhatsApp after the owner approves, with an alternate-vendor suggestion if the usual vendor is late.
Flags which suppliers are MSME-registered (Udyam) and shows each vendor's 45-day payment due date, so the weekly purchase and payment plan avoids 43B(h) disallowance.
Posts a daily 'orders at risk' digest to the owner's Telegram or WhatsApp, with the one purchase that would unblock the most rupees of orders.
agents.price_inr: ₹2,999/month (up to 300 SKUs); ₹15,000 one-time done-for-you Tally setup
agents.beyond_baseline: Starts from the customer's PO and works backward to shortages and a delivery promise, instead of stock-level alerts. It also folds MSME payment-term compliance into the purchasing decision.
agents.wow_moment: Forward a customer's PO PDF to a WhatsApp number. 30 seconds later a reply says: 'Can ship 240 pcs by 18 Mar, not 12 Mar. Short: 38 kg EN8 bar, 400 M6 bolts. RFQs drafted for 2 vendors. Tap to send.'
agents.integrations: Tally Prime (XML/ODBC export via a local connector), Zoho Inventory API, Google Sheets/Excel BOMs, WhatsApp Business Cloud API, Telegram, Udyam/GSTIN lookup
agents.stack: Python FastAPI, Claude vision/PDF extraction, Postgres, a small Tally XML sync agent in Docker, WhatsApp Cloud API, React admin for BOM mapping
agents.first_customers: Contact auto-ancillary and fabrication MSMEs in Hyderabad (Jeedimetla, Balanagar, Cherlapally industrial areas) via local industry associations and the agency's network. Offer a free 'send me 3 old POs' audit.
agents.risks: Tally data hygiene and messy BOMs slow onboarding. Wrong BOM mapping gives false confidence, so keep a human approval step and show the matching confidence. WhatsApp template approval is needed for outbound vendor messages.

agents.one_liner: A pre-flight and in-flight check that stops email, WhatsApp and ad campaigns from promoting SKUs that will sell out before the campaign finishes.
agents.buyer: CRM or growth manager at an Indian D2C brand or multi-store retailer (fashion, beauty, home, electronics) using Shopify or Unicommerce with WebEngage, MoEngage, Klaviyo or Meta Ads. The agency can also sell it as a retainer add-on.
agents.problem: CRM teams schedule a sale blast featuring hero SKUs. Inventory and merchandising teams don't know the send time. The campaign then drives demand to out-of-stock or single-size-left items, which wastes send cost, ad spend and customer trust. Stock tools only look at replenishment, and campaign tools never look at stock. Note: no market-signal URLs were supplied in the prompt, so none are cited.
what_it_does: Pulls the campaign calendar and product blocks from the ESP or CRM (Klaviyo, WebEngage, MoEngage, or a Google Sheet) and the live SKU, size and store or pincode inventory from Shopify or Unicommerce.
Forecasts, from past campaign lift per segment and size, when each promoted SKU will stock out after send, and gives a pre-flight risk score for the campaign.
Suggests substitutes by category, price band, margin and available size curve, and rewrites the product block or Klaviyo product feed for approval.
During the send, polls sell-through every 15 minutes. It can pause the Meta ad set for a stocked-out SKU, or swap the dynamic content in later email or WhatsApp batches.
Sends a post-campaign report on rupees lost to stockouts and clicks that hit out-of-stock pages, so merchandising can see the gap and buy deeper next time.
agents.price_inr: ₹7,999/month per brand; agency plan ₹24,999/month for 5 brands
agents.beyond_baseline: The trigger is a scheduled marketing campaign, not a stock threshold. It links the demand-creation side (CRM) with the supply side, and few tools cover both.
agents.wow_moment: Open a scheduled Diwali email. Three of the five hero products are marked red: 'Sells out 41 minutes after send.' One click swaps in in-stock lookalikes, and the forecast flips to green.
agents.integrations: Shopify Admin API, Unicommerce, Klaviyo, WebEngage, MoEngage, Meta Marketing API, Google Sheets, Slack/Telegram
agents.stack: Python workers on GitHub Actions or a cron container, Claude for substitution reasoning and copy edits, React dashboard, Postgres, Shopify webhooks
agents.first_customers: Mid-size Shopify D2C brands and the agency's own enterprise-retail CRM contacts. Pitch with a free audit of the last 3 campaigns showing estimated stockout losses.
agents.risks: Write access to ESPs and ad accounts needs trust. Start in read-only recommend mode. Forecast quality is limited when campaign history is thin, so use conservative bands and explain them. Each ESP API differs, so start with Klaviyo and Shopify.

agents.one_liner: Finds batches heading for expiry in a pharma or FMCG stockist's Marg or Busy stock and turns them into WhatsApp offers to the right retailers before the company-return window closes.
agents.buyer: Owner or accountant at a pharma, FMCG or nutrition distributor (stockist) with 1-5 godowns, running Marg ERP, Busy or Tally, supplying 100-1,500 chemists and kirana retailers.
agents.problem: Distributors lose money on near-expiry and short-dated batches. Principal companies accept expiry returns only within set windows and under claim conditions, and chemists refuse short-dated stock. Batch data sits in Marg and nobody reviews it by retailer demand. Salesmen offload stock informally and the claim paperwork gets missed. Note: no market-signal URLs were supplied in the prompt, so none are cited.
what_it_does: Ingests a daily Marg, Busy or Tally batch-wise stock export and ranks batches by days to expiry, rupees at risk, and each principal's return-acceptance window or rules (configured per company).
Matches each at-risk batch to retailers who bought that SKU or salt in the last 6 months and sell through fast enough, and proposes a discount using margin and expected return value.
Drafts personalised WhatsApp offers in the local language for owner or salesman approval, then collects 'yes' replies and creates the sales-order draft with batch and expiry noted.
Prepares the expiry-return claim pack for items that won't sell (batch, MRP, purchase invoice, GST credit-note details) before the company deadline.
Updates purchasing: reduces reorder suggestions for SKUs that keep expiring, and shows a monthly expiry-loss report by principal.
agents.price_inr: ₹3,499/month per godown; ₹12,000 one-time onboarding
agents.beyond_baseline: It handles stock that has to leave, not stock that is missing. It works at batch, expiry and retailer level and closes the loop with offers and return claims, which generic replenishment tools don't do.
agents.wow_moment: Upload a Marg batch-stock Excel. In 10 seconds: '₹4.8 lakh at risk in the next 90 days. 11 chemists are ready to buy ₹2.1 lakh of it. Offers are drafted. Approve all.'
agents.integrations: Marg ERP (Excel/CSV export, later DB sync), Busy, Tally Prime, WhatsApp Business Cloud API, Google Sheets, GST credit-note formats, Telegram for salesman approvals
agents.stack: Python (pandas) pipeline, Claude for multilingual message drafts and column mapping across export formats, FastAPI, React, WhatsApp Cloud API, Docker on VPS
agents.first_customers: Pharma stockists in Hyderabad (Koti, Begum Bazar, Secunderabad) and FMCG sub-distributors, reached through chemist association WhatsApp groups. Offer a free one-off expiry scan on one export.
agents.risks: Marg export formats vary by version. Start with CSV upload. Principals' return rules differ and change, so keep them configurable and verified by the user. WhatsApp marketing opt-in and template rules apply to retailer messaging, and pharma discounting may have regulatory limits.

agents.one_liner: A GitHub-native bot that finds a leaked cloud or payment key, checks whether it still works, and revokes it from a Telegram tap. It then drafts the CERT-In incident note.
agents.buyer: CTO or founding engineer at a 5-100 person Indian SaaS, fintech or app-dev agency with no security team. Also dev agencies that hold their clients' keys.
agents.problem: Indian startups and agencies routinely push AWS keys, Razorpay/PayU secrets, Firebase service accounts, Twilio and OpenAI keys to GitHub, often in public or forked repos. Generic secret scanners (GitHub secret scanning, Gitleaks, TruffleHog) produce a flood of alerts. They don't say whether a key is live, whether anyone has used it, or what to do next. CERT-In's April 2022 directive requires reporting certain incidents within 6 hours, and no small team has that process ready.
what_it_does: Installs as a GitHub App plus Action. It scans every push, PR, fork and gist for the org's members, and checks commit history for deleted secrets.
Verifies each finding safely with read-only calls such as AWS STS GetCallerIdentity, Razorpay key ping and Firebase token checks. It labels each one LIVE, DEAD or UNKNOWN.
For a LIVE key, it sends a Telegram/Slack card with the key owner, the repo, the scopes found, and recent usage (CloudTrail look-back). One tap approves revoke or rotate through the provider API.
Opens an auto-fix PR that moves the secret to env/GitHub Secrets and adds a pre-commit hook. It then scrubs history with a git-filter-repo command it generates for the dev.
Produces a CERT-In-style incident draft with timeline, blast radius and actions taken. It also writes a plain-language client notice for agencies.
Sends a weekly 'secret hygiene' score per developer and repo, to justify the retainer.

agents.integrations: GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket, AWS (STS/IAM/CloudTrail), GCP/Firebase, Razorpay, Stripe, Twilio, OpenAI/Anthropic keys, Slack, Telegram, Jira

agents.one_liner: An impersonation-takedown agent for SEBI-registered brokers, RIAs and research analysts. It hunts fake 'VIP stock tip' Telegram/WhatsApp groups, lookalike domains and cloned APKs, then files the takedowns.
agents.buyer: Compliance officer or CISO at small and mid-size stock brokers and sub-brokers, SEBI-registered RIAs/RAs, AMFI mutual fund distributors, and NBFC/loan-app brands. Also the founder of a SEBI RA with a big Telegram following.
agents.problem: Fraudsters clone Indian broker and advisor brands. They run fake 'XYZ Securities Institutional VIP' WhatsApp/Telegram groups, fake trading apps shared as APKs, and lookalike domains. Customers lose money and blame the real brand. SEBI has repeatedly warned about this, and brokers and RAs are expected to run cyber-resilience programmes under SEBI's CSCRF. Brand-protection tools from global vendors cost lakhs and don't cover Telegram or WhatsApp invite links, or Indian reporting channels. Compliance teams currently do this by hand with screenshots.
what_it_does: Continuously watches for the brand, its SEBI registration number, the CEO's name and the product names. Sources are public Telegram channel search, WhatsApp invite links surfaced from Google/X/YouTube comments, new-domain feeds (typosquat permutations, certificate transparency logs), and APK-sharing sites.
Classifies each hit as scam, fan page or legit using an LLM over text, logo and claims such as 'guaranteed 300% returns', and a check against the SEBI intermediary registry.
Captures timestamped evidence packs: screenshots, WHOIS, hosting, admin handles and APK hash.
Drafts takedown submissions with a human approve button: registrar abuse, Telegram abuse, Cloudflare/host, Google Play/Safe Browsing, CERT-In, cybercrime.gov.in and a SEBI SCORES-style complaint.
Sends warning posts for the brand's own channels (WhatsApp broadcast, X, email) in English, Hindi and Telugu: 'we have no VIP group, here are our real handles'.
Produces a monthly board/SEBI-audit-ready report with number of threats found, takedown time and estimated customers exposed.
agents.price_inr: ₹14,999/mo mid-size broker; ₹4,999/mo solo RA/RIA; ₹40,000 one-time brand audit
agents.beyond_baseline: The baseline is triaging internal alerts. This one covers external threats where Indian finance actually bleeds (Telegram and WhatsApp scams) and ends in evidence plus a filed complaint, which ties into SEBI/CERT-In compliance.
agents.wow_moment: Type a broker's brand name. In 60 seconds the screen shows a live map of 7 fake Telegram groups, 3 lookalike domains registered this week and 1 cloned APK, each with a one-click 'Generate takedown pack' button producing a ready PDF.
agents.stack: Python scrapers and Telethon for public-channel search, dnstwist, crt.sh, WHOIS APIs, Playwright for screenshots, Claude vision and text for classification, Laravel or React admin, Telegram bot for approvals, Docker on the VPS
agents.integrations: Telegram, WhatsApp Business (for the brand's warning broadcasts), SEBI intermediary registry, Cloudflare/registrar abuse forms, CERT-In and cybercrime.gov.in (draft only), Google Safe Browsing, Slack/email
agents.first_customers: Small and mid-size brokers and sub-broker networks, SEBI RAs and RIAs with large YouTube and Telegram audiences (the builder's stock-market network), and NSE/BSE-registered authorised persons. Start with a free 'brand exposure scan' sent to compliance heads on LinkedIn.

False positives hurt trust, so run a precision-first rollout. Sales to brokers can be slow, so lead with RAs and RIAs.

agents.one_liner: A watchdog for the marketing stack of an enterprise retailer. It catches customer-list exports, rogue API keys and email-domain spoofing across the CRM and ESP, and writes the DPDP breach notice if needed.
agents.buyer: CISO or DPO at a mid-to-large Indian retail, D2C or BFSI-adjacent enterprise. A secondary buyer is the head of CRM/marketing ops, who is accountable for the data but has no security tooling.
agents.problem: A retailer's most valuable and least guarded data sits in the CRM/ESP: millions of customer emails and phone numbers. Agencies, freelancers and interns hold export rights. API keys sprawl across Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Netcore, Braze, MoEngage, WebEngage and Mailchimp. Nobody watches for a 3 a.m. 500k-row export, a new sender domain, or a DMARC failure spike that signals spoofing. Under the DPDP Act 2023 a personal-data breach must be reported to the Data Protection Board and affected users. SIEMs ignore these systems, and security teams don't understand campaign operations.
what_it_does: Pulls audit and event logs from the CRM/ESP (Salesforce event monitoring, SFMC audit, Netcore/MoEngage logs, Google Workspace) and builds a baseline per user: export size, time, IP, segment type.
Flags risky patterns: bulk exports, segment-to-file downloads, new API keys or webhooks, a user outside their agency's contract window, and PII-heavy fields in a campaign test list.
Monitors SPF, DKIM and DMARC alignment, DMARC aggregate (rua) reports, dangling subdomains and lookalike sending domains, to catch phishing in the brand's name before a big sale campaign.
On a high-severity event, sends a WhatsApp/Teams/Slack card with who, what, how many data principals, which fields, and one-tap actions: suspend the user, revoke the key, pause the send.
Drafts the DPDP incident package: timeline, data categories, affected-count estimate, a draft notice to customers and a board summary. It also drafts a CERT-In 6-hour report when relevant.
Gives marketing ops a monthly 'least privilege' report listing stale agency accounts and over-permissioned users, with approval-based cleanup.
agents.price_inr: ₹30,000/mo per brand; ₹1.5L one-time pilot with an integration setup and a 30-day data-access audit
agents.beyond_baseline: Standard SOC agents triage endpoint and network alerts. This one understands campaign-ops semantics (segments, journeys, suppression lists, agency access) and turns the security signal into a DPDP-ready response that marketing ops can act on.
agents.wow_moment: In a demo CRM, a freelancer account exports a 4.2 lakh-customer segment at 2:07 a.m. Ten seconds later the CISO's WhatsApp lights up with 'Export of 4.2L records with email, phone, city. Suspend user?'. One tap suspends the account, and the DPDP draft notice appears.
agents.stack: Python collectors and schedulers, Postgres, Claude API for summarising events and drafting notices, a React/Three.js dashboard (a 3D data-flow map of systems and agencies is a good visual), WhatsApp Business API, Telegram/Slack, dmarc-parser, Docker on the VPS
agents.integrations: Salesforce and Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Netcore, MoEngage, WebEngage, Braze, Mailchimp, Google Workspace/Microsoft 365 audit logs, Slack/Teams, WhatsApp Business, DMARC rua reports
agents.first_customers: The builder's own enterprise retail CRM network and former colleagues in campaign ops. Then CRM/martech agencies that can resell it as an 'agency access audit' to their retail clients, and a few DPOs found through DPDP-readiness LinkedIn events.
agents.risks: Enterprise sales cycles are long, and security reviews of an app that reads their logs are heavy. Starting with a read-only audit pilot reduces friction. Each connector needs maintenance, so launch with 2 platforms (Salesforce and one Indian ESP). DPDP rules are still being operationalised, so the notice templates must be flagged as drafts for legal review.

agents.one_liner: Reads a listed company's last 8 earnings calls and filings, then flags where management's promises drifted from the reported numbers, with page-level citations.
agents.buyer: Boutique strategy and management consultants, PE/VC associates, and equity research freelancers in India who must get up to speed on a listed client or target in 48 hours.
agents.problem: On a new engagement or a deal screen, an analyst spends 2 to 3 days reading concall transcripts, annual reports and BSE/NSE announcements to find what management said versus what happened. what_it_does: Pulls the last 8 to 12 concall transcripts, investor presentations and annual reports for a ticker from BSE/NSE corporate announcements, and extracts forward-looking statements such as capex, margin guidance, order book and debt reduction.

Builds a benchmark table against 3 to 5 peers on the same promise categories.

Sends a Telegram or WhatsApp alert when a new concall posts that changes an earlier flag.

agents.one_liner: Upload a draft petition, reply or opinion. It checks that every cited case exists and is still good law, and converts old IPC/CrPC/Evidence Act references to BNS/BNSS/BSA with post-July-2024 authority.
agents.buyer: Junior advocates, small litigation firms (2 to 15 lawyers) and in-house counsel in India, who are drafting under the new criminal codes while most precedent still cites IPC and CrPC.
agents.problem: Since 1 July 2024, drafts mix IPC/CrPC/IEA with BNS/BNSS/BSA. Section mappings are error-prone, and pleadings are increasingly caught with hallucinated or misquoted citations. Courts have started noticing AI-fabricated cases. Lawyers need a verifier, not another drafter.
what_it_does: Parses an uploaded DOCX or PDF draft and extracts every statute section and case citation, such as AIR, SCC and neutral citations.

Verifies each case against Indian Kanoon and Supreme Court or High Court public judgment sources, confirming the party names, year, bench and quoted paragraph. Anything not found is flagged 'could not verify'.
Maps IPC, CrPC and IEA sections to BNS, BNSS and BSA equivalents, notes substantive changes, and flags where old precedent needs a 'read with' note.
Checks subsequent treatment (followed, distinguished, overruled) using citing judgments, and suggests 3 to 5 post-July-2024 cases on the same section.
Returns a tracked-changes DOCX with margin comments plus a one-page verification report. The advocate accepts or rejects each change.
Offers a WhatsApp or Telegram quick mode: send 'Sec 420 IPC' and get the BNS 318 mapping with the key changes.
agents.price_inr: ₹999/month individual advocate; ₹6,999/month small firm; ₹199 per document pay-as-you-go
agents.beyond_baseline: Existing legal research tools answer questions. This audits your own draft line by line and treats unverifiable citations as the product, which matches the real fear of embarrassment before the bench.
agents.wow_moment: Drop in a 15-page bail application. Seconds later the Word file shows 3 yellow comments: 'Citation not found: likely fabricated', 'Sec 438 CrPC → Sec 482 BNSS (new proviso added)' and 'Case overruled in 2023, see ...'.
agents.first_customers: Hyderabad and Telangana High Court junior advocates via bar association WhatsApp groups, criminal-law practitioners, law-school moot and clinic networks, and legal-tech LinkedIn and X.
agents.integrations: Indian Kanoon API, India Code, eCourts and Supreme Court judgment portals, Microsoft Word (DOCX tracked changes), WhatsApp Business, Telegram, Google Drive
agents.stack: Python and FastAPI, python-docx and docx XML for tracked changes, a regex plus LLM citation extractor, a curated IPC to BNS mapping table checked by a lawyer, Claude API, React upload UI, Docker on the VPS
agents.risks: Indian Kanoon API terms and cost per call. The mapping table must be lawyer-reviewed. Bar Council advertising rules, so position it as a tool and not legal advice. Citation formats vary. Never show a green tick unless the match is exact. No market-signal URLs were supplied in the prompt, so none are cited.

agents.one_liner: Drop a tender technical specification and a vendor datasheet. It returns a clause-by-clause compliance matrix with deviations, citing the exact lines of both documents.

Compares multiple vendors side by side and highlights the cheapest technically compliant bidder using the supplied commercial sheet.

agents.one_liner: Paste an invention disclosure. It runs a prior-art sweep across patents and papers and returns an element-by-element claim chart showing exactly where novelty is at risk.
agents.buyer: Indian patent agents, IP boutiques, university tech-transfer offices and deep-tech or pharma R&D teams who must judge novelty and inventive step before spending ₹1 lakh or more on filing.
agents.problem: A prior-art search takes a patent agent 1 to 3 days across Google Patents, Lens, Espacenet and InPASS. Founders often file without searching, and Indian examination (FER under Section 12/13) then surfaces citations that kill claims. Existing tools return lists of similar patents, not an argument-ready analysis.
what_it_does: Turns the disclosure into a structured set of claim elements and generates keyword, CPC/IPC and semantic queries.
Searches Lens.org, Espacenet OPS, Google Patents public data, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar, then deduplicates by patent family.
Ranks the 10 to 15 closest references and builds a claim chart. Each element is marked disclosed, partially disclosed or absent, with a quoted passage and paragraph number.
Highlights the 'white space', meaning the elements that no reference discloses, and suggests claim-narrowing options for the agent's review.
Produces a Word report in a familiar search-report format and a short founder-friendly verdict. Also drafts a response outline when an FER citation is pasted in.
Sets a watch that sends a Telegram alert when a new publication overlaps with a saved disclosure.
agents.price_inr: ₹4,999/month agent plan (15 searches); ₹1,999 per search report; ₹49,999/year for university TTO
agents.beyond_baseline: It does not return a list of similar documents. It outputs the claim-chart reasoning that a patent professional would write, with quotes, and keeps a live watch on the invention.
agents.wow_moment: Paste a 300-word idea for a battery thermal-management design. 90 seconds later a colour-coded chart appears: 4 elements are covered by US patent X (para 0042), 1 element has no reference, and that one is the claim to lead with.
agents.first_customers: Independent patent agents and small IP firms in Hyderabad, Pune and Bengaluru, IIT and IIIT incubators' TTOs, and pharma formulation startups in Genome Valley.
agents.integrations: Lens.org API, Espacenet OPS, Google Patents public datasets, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, InPASS (manual import), Word, Zotero, Telegram
agents.stack: Python orchestration, embeddings with pgvector, Claude API for query generation and claim charting, python-docx, React UI, GitHub Actions for watch jobs, Docker on the VPS
agents.risks: Not a legal opinion, since only a registered patent agent can advise, so sell it as an assistant to them. API rate limits and licensing for Lens. Indian patent data via InPASS has no clean API. Confidentiality worries, so offer a no-training, delete-after-30-days policy. No market-signal URLs were supplied in the prompt, so none are cited.
